name: Orgasm-Induced Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Reflex Epilepsy with Orgasmic Trigger

criteria.description: Recurrent seizures consistently triggered by orgasm or sexual activity
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing epileptiform discharges during or immediately after orgasmic events
Exclusion of other seizure triggers and non-epileptic causes
Neuroimaging (MRI) may show focal abnormalities in temporal or frontal lobes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent orgasm-triggered seizures confirmed by clinical history and EEG findings, with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful differentiation from psychogenic non-epileptic seizures and other reflex epilepsies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal impaired awareness seizures during sexual climax

common.symptomName: Aura with epigastric rising sensation preceding seizure
searchTerms: seizure warning with rising stomach feeling

common.symptomName: Automatisms such as lip-smacking or manual automatisms during seizure
Postictal confusion lasting minutes to hours

occasional.symptomName: Generalized tonic-clonic seizures unrelated to sexual activity
searchTerms: full body convulsions not linked to sex
generalized seizures unrelated to sexual activity

occasional.symptomName: Anxiety related to anticipation of seizures during sexual activity
searchTerms: anxiety about having seizures during sex
fear of seizures with sexual activity

occasional.symptomName: Transient aphasia or speech arrest during seizures
searchTerms: temporary loss of speech during seizure

rare.symptomName: Autonomic symptoms including flushing and palpitations during seizures
searchTerms: flushing and fast heartbeat during seizures
autonomic symptoms like palpitations in seizures
seeing things that aren't there before seizure
seeing flashes or images before seizure
temporary loss of bladder control during seizure

imaging: MRI may reveal focal cortical dysplasia or mesial temporal sclerosis
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible familial predisposition in rare cases
other: Video-EEG monitoring captures seizures triggered by orgasmic stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of epileptiform EEG changes during events
Variable triggers not consistently linked to orgasm
Seizures triggered by multiple stimuli, not exclusively orgasm
MRI findings of mesial temporal sclerosis

redFlags: Seizure onset during sexual activity with loss of consciousness
Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) risk
Seizures refractory to standard antiepileptic drugs
references: Fisher RS, et al. Epileptic seizures and epilepsy: definitions proposed by the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) and the International Bureau for Epilepsy (IBE). Epilepsia. 2014.
Koepp MJ, et al. Reflex epilepsy: clinical and neurophysiological features. Epilepsia. 2016.
